title: Base 7
statement: Write the integer `num` in base 7 and return the result as a string. Use the digits `0` to `6` with no leading zeros (zero itself is `"0"`), and put a `-` in front when `num` is negative.
notes:
## Intuition

In base 7, the last digit of a number is its remainder when divided by 7, and dividing by 7 (dropping the remainder) removes that digit. Repeating "take the remainder, then divide" peels the digits off from right to left, exactly like writing a number in base 10 by repeatedly dividing by 10. The sign is handled separately: convert the absolute value and put `-` in front. A slower alternative finds the largest power of 7 that fits and counts how many times each power can be subtracted.

## Approach

1. Zero has no digits to peel off, so return `"0"` straight away.
2. Remember whether `num` is `negative`, and work with its absolute value `value`.
3. While `value > 0`, take `digit = value % 7` and put it in front of `digits`.
4. Replace `value` with `Math.floor(value / 7)`.
5. Return `digits`, with a `-` in front when the input was negative.

## Example 1, step by step

`num = 100`. First `100 % 7 = 2`, so `digits = "2"`, and `value` becomes `14`. Next `14 % 7 = 0` gives `"02"`, and `value` becomes `2`. Finally `2 % 7 = 2` gives `"202"`, and `value` becomes `0`. Check: `2·49 + 0·7 + 2 = 100`. The answer is `"202"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(log₇ |num|): one step per base-7 digit, at most 9 for `|num| <= 10^7`.
- Space: O(log₇ |num|) for the digit string.

## Pitfalls

- Without the special case, `0` would produce an empty string.
- In JavaScript, `-7 % 7` is `-0` and `-8 % 7` is `-1`: take the absolute value first instead of dividing a negative number.
- Digits come out in reverse order, so prepend each one (or reverse at the end).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `negative` | whether `num` was below zero |
| `value` | the part of `|num|` whose digits are not written yet |
| `digit` | the current lowest base-7 digit |
| `digits` | the base-7 digits written so far, most significant first |

narration.2: Zero is a special case: the loop below would write no digits for it.
narration.5: Note the sign now so it can be added back at the end.
narration.6: Convert the absolute value; the sign does not change the digits.
narration.7: The digits will be built up here.
narration.8: Keep going while some digits are still unwritten.
narration.9: The remainder by 7 is the lowest base-7 digit.
narration.10: Each new digit is more significant than those already written, so it goes in front.
narration.11: Dividing by 7 drops the digit just written.
narration.13: Put back the minus sign for a negative input.
